Subject: 2030 Q3 Downtown Commercial Ecology and Street Pedestrian Flow Statistics Plan 
To all Commercial District Management Committees and related merchants: 
To further optimize the spatial layout of the downtown commercial district and improve the 
quality of public services, the Department of Urban Planning and Economic Development will 
conduct comprehensive statistics work on commercial ecology and pedestrian flow in the third 
quarter of 2030 (August 1 to October 31). 
This statistics aims to collect the following core data: 
1.​ Pedestrian flow fluctuation curves of core commercial streets (including Rue des Myosotis 
and its surrounding radiating areas) during different time periods (weekdays, weekends, 
and holidays). 
2.​ Preliminary assessment of the distribution density and operating conditions of existing 
retail, catering, and service merchants. 
3.​ Usage frequency of public resting facilities (such as benches, small plazas). 
To ensure the objectivity and accuracy of the data, we will commission a third-party research 
agency to use a combination of manual counting and automatic sensing equipment. 
Researchers will wear identification badges uniformly issued by the municipality and carry out 
their work on the premise of not affecting the normal operation of merchants and pedestrian 
traffic. 
We sincerely call on all merchants to understand and cooperate with this statistics plan. If you 
have any questions, please contact the Economic Development Section through the municipal 
service platform (Portail Citoyen).

Subject: Summary of Routine Monitoring of Air Quality and Noise Pollution in Major 
Commercial Streets for June 2030 
Overview: 
This report summarizes the air quality index (AQI) of the central area of Sainte-Hélène town and 
the noise pollution monitoring results of major commercial streets (focusing on Rue Jean 
Jaurès, Rue des Myosotis, and Place de la Mairie) from June 1 to June 30, 2030. 
1. Air Quality (Qualité de l'air): 
In June, the overall air quality of the town remained at an "Excellent" to "Good" level. Due to 
significantly more precipitation than the same period in previous years, the concentration of 
inhalable particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5) was significantly lower than the legal control 
standards. Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) concentrations rose slightly during morning and evening 
peak hours, but the all-day averages were within the safe range. No ozone (O3) exceedance 
warnings were issued. 
2. Noise Pollution (Nuisances sonores): 
Fixed-point monitoring of core commercial streets found: 
●​ Daytime (07:00 - 22:00): The average noise level was 62 decibels, and the main noise 
sources were motor vehicle traffic, commercial activities, and pedestrian conversations. 
The southern section of Rue des Myosotis experienced brief noise peaks (up to 75 decibels) 
due to minor internal renovations by some merchants, but all were controlled within the 
permitted time periods. 
●​ Nighttime (22:00 - 07:00): The average noise level dropped below 45 decibels, complying 
with the town's protection regulations for a tranquil nighttime environment. Slight 
exceedances were recorded only around individual bars on weekends, which have been 
handed over to the municipal police department for follow-up processing. 
The Department of Environment will continue to maintain regular monitoring, committed to 
providing a healthy and comfortable urban environment for citizens and merchants. The full 
report is available for review in the public reading room on the first floor of the City Hall.

Subject: Latest Regulations on Strengthening Commercial Garbage Classification for Street 
Merchants and Adjusting Scheduled Clearing Times 
To all street merchants and operators in the town: 
In order to implement the latest national environmental protection policies on circular economy 
and waste reduction, and improve the appearance and environment of the town, the Office of 
Urban Cleanliness and Waste Management has decided to fully implement stricter commercial 
garbage classification and clearing management new regulations starting from August 1, 2030. 
I. Mandatory Classification Requirements: 
All merchants must strictly store waste separately according to the following categories: 
1.​ Recyclables (Yellow Bin): Limited to clean cardboard, plastic packaging, metal cans, etc. 
Special reminder: Cardboard boxes must be flattened before being put in. It is strictly 
forbidden to pile unflattened cardboard boxes outside the bin. 
2.​ Glass Products (Green Bin): Limited to glass bottles and jars, please empty the contents. 
3.​ Organic Waste (Brown Bin): For catering and related merchants, kitchen waste must be 
separated. 
4.​ Other non-recyclable garbage (Grey/Black Bin). 
II. Clearing Time Adjustment (Special Regulations for Historic Districts): 
To reduce the impact of garbage truck operations on commercial activities and tourist 
experience, the garbage clearing time for merchants located in historic districts (including Rue 
des Myosotis, Ruelle des Artisans, etc.) is adjusted to: 
●​ Morning Shift: 05:30 to 07:00 
●​ Evening Shift: 22:30 to 23:30 
Merchants must and can only push the corresponding garbage bins to the designated 
area in front of the door within 30 minutes before the start of the above clearing time 
periods. After the clearing is completed, the garbage bins must be taken back into the 
store within 1 hour. Long-term occupation of public sidewalks is strictly prohibited. 
Improper waste classification or bin placement will result in municipal warnings. Repeated 
offenses carry fines of €135 to €750. Thank you for cooperating.

forbidden to pile unflattened cardboard boxes outside the bin.

offenses carry fines of €135 to €750. Thank you for cooperating.
